Hello to desk staff,
The training lead asked me to write about staff rotas

We need sharper coverage across the Companion Animal Travel Desk, because delayed replies and uneven handoffs are already creating avoidable pressure. Keep the tone calm, keep the guidance clear, and treat every passenger message as urgent until it is resolved. When a case moves from intake to transfer, follow the current workflow exactly. <<FACT F094>> Do not leave notes half done, and do not assume another colleague has already updated the record. If you are moving a case on, make the handoff obvious and complete.

For incident reporting, use the established route without delay and record the details while they are still fresh. <<FACT F102>> If a passenger raises a concern about a carrier, a document, or a companion animal's comfort, capture the facts in plain language and flag anything that could affect onward travel. Check your own queue at the start of each shift and again before you hand over. We cannot afford loose ends, missed acknowledgements, or duplicate promises to customers. If Samuel Adeyemi or Lucia Adeyemi appears in a case file, read the history before replying, and keep any reference to Winston consistent with the file notes. Prompt, respectful communication is expected from everyone.

Please review your rota coverage, confirm your assignment, and speak up early if you see a gap that could affect the day. If you are unsure which step comes next, ask before acting. Clear communication protects passengers, protects animals, and protects the desk from escalation. Stay ready, stay accurate, and keep the workflow moving.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
